evidence: Actual final Chat input capture is used in the positive local test; quote and admission receipts are test doubles.
The six-field Service Binding envelope invokes the real v384/v365 holder and makes exactly one POST to an owned 127.0.0.1 server.
Quote/admission ACK failure, plan/Guardrail/identity mutation, and post-send Binding failure block a second local send or preserve an unknown obligation.
The second-instance pending_unknown result and ordinary/Guardrail hold states are simulated SQL outcomes, not native PostgreSQL evidence in this fixture.
Only 200 SSE or JSON body is returned, with Provider/private headers removed; this does not reproduce all real Chat error and metadata behavior.
limitations: No real Chat route calls this module; current opt-in route still uses the legacy budget owner and proxy.
v360 and v361 client/SQL behavior has separate PostgreSQL evidence, but no combined native PostgreSQL and Worker Service Binding run covers v385.
The public Gateway currently retains its existing shared-key encryption binding; this module adds no provider KEK port but does not prove deployed secret separation.
No trusted Provider bill, complete zero-charge authority, final financial closer, D1/MySQL parity or paid Provider call is established.
OpenRouter-specific server-owned user correlation, generation ID observation, and cross-key/echo behavior are not established.
